item_packs.description: Details for data passed as files: media type, serialization, schema, compression, checksum, and staging.
Which assay produced the data: protocol, instrument, calibration, and controls.
Where the data comes from biologically: species, material, disease, intervention, assay, and compartment.
Which cells the data describes: cell type, lineage, culture conditions, passage, and state.
Rules for clinical data: coding systems, population, consent, de-identification, and use restrictions.
How an array is laid out: named axes, coordinates, labels, sizes, and order.
Dose-response data: the intervention, dose axis, endpoint, response direction, and fitted curve.
Sample-by-feature matrices, including exactly which features are present and how the data was preprocessed.
Networks: node and edge types, direction, weights, sources, and identifier systems.
Versioned identifiers, normalized so the same thing always gets the same ID.
Images and volumes: pixels or voxels, channels, resolution, registration, and anatomical frame.
Mappings between identifier systems: the exact source and target systems, and a fixed record of the mapping used.
What was measured: quantity, unit, scale, normalization, and detection limits.
Which molecule this is: chemical or macromolecular structure, stereochemistry, charge, and conformer.
Ontology terms pinned to a specific version, and safe rules for matching broader and narrower terms.
Pharmacokinetics: exposure, sampling times, compartments, and PK parameter definitions.
Which population the data describes: strata, geography, denominator, sampling frame, and rates.
The port fields model.yaml already has (name, type, shape), carried into the contract.
Where a value came from and how it was produced.
How the data is encoded and structured.
What travels with a value at run time: context, the value or file itself, provenance, and observation time.
How the data may be handled: classification, license, consent, data residency, and workspace policy.
What the data means, biologically or computationally.
Sequence positions: alphabet, strand, coordinates, and reference genome assembly.
What you need to rerun a simulation: model formalism, solver, tolerances, random seed, and state order.
Taxonomy and evolution: lineage, phylogenetic method, evolutionary time, and confidence.
Timing: how states and events change over time, sampling, and how recent the data is.
Data quality: uncertainty, confidence, quality flags, missing values, and censoring.
Validation rules written as data, never as code.
Genetic variants: normalized variant identity and predicted consequence.

profiles.name: protein-sequence
profiles.label: Protein Sequence
profiles.description: An amino-acid residue sequence representing a declared protein or polypeptide, with the identifier namespace, namespace version and organism context needed to interpret it.
profiles.compatibility_notes: Two ports match only when every field the target port requires is satisfied. If required information is missing, the result is UNKNOWN. Any conversion between ports must be a declared, versioned transformation.
profiles.scientific_claim: This profile checks whether two model interfaces fit together. It doesn't show that a model is scientifically valid or clinically safe.

profiles.name: protein-structure
profiles.label: Protein Structure
profiles.description: A three-dimensional structural representation of a declared protein or protein-containing assembly, including the identity, coordinate representation and format needed to interpret the structure.
profiles.compatibility_notes: Two ports match only when every field the target port requires is satisfied. If required information is missing, the result is UNKNOWN. Any conversion between ports must be a declared, versioned transformation.
profiles.scientific_claim: This profile checks whether two model interfaces fit together. It doesn't show that a model is scientifically valid or clinically safe.

profiles.name: canonical-smiles
profiles.label: Canonical SMILES
profiles.description: A SMILES representation designated canonical by a declared canonicalization method, software implementation and version for a specified chemical structure.
profiles.compatibility_notes: Two ports match only when every field the target port requires is satisfied. If required information is missing, the result is UNKNOWN. Any conversion between ports must be a declared, versioned transformation.
profiles.scientific_claim: This profile checks whether two model interfaces fit together. It doesn't show that a model is scientifically valid or clinically safe.
